regulatory_clause: (2) The existing products which are not complying with the IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 and this Master Circular shall be modified on or before 30.09.2024.
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must modify existing products to comply with new regulations within 153 days of the circular issue.

regulatory_clause: A period of 30 days (from the date of receipt of the policy document) is available to the policyholder to review the terms and conditions of the policy.
plain_english_explanation: Policyholders have 30 days to review and cancel their policy after receiving the policy document.

regulatory_clause: The policyholder may cancel his/her policy at any time during the term, by giving 7 days notice in writing.
plain_english_explanation: Policyholders must give 7 days' notice in writing to cancel their policy.

regulatory_clause: The grace period of fifteen days (where premium is paid on a monthly instalments) is available on the premium due date, to pay the premium.
plain_english_explanation: Policyholders have 15 days to pay their monthly premium after the due date.

regulatory_clause: The grace period of thirty days (where premium is paid in quarterly/half-yearly/annual instalments) is available on the premium due date, to pay the premium.
plain_english_explanation: Policyholders have 30 days to pay their quarterly, half-yearly, or annual premium after the due date.

regulatory_clause: The existing insurer shall provide the information sought by the Acquiring insurer immediately but not more than 72 hours of receipt of request through Insurance Information Bureau of India (IIB) https://iib.gov.in/ portal.
plain_english_explanation: Existing insurers must transfer underwriting details to the acquiring insurer within 72 hours of request.

regulatory_clause: The Acquiring insurer shall decide and communicate on the proposal immediately but not more than 5 days of receipt of information from Existing insurer.
plain_english_explanation: Acquiring insurers must decide on portability proposals within 5 days of receiving information from the existing insurer.

regulatory_clause: b. Insurer shall decide on the request for cashless authorization immediately but not more than one hour of receipt of request.
plain_english_explanation: The insurer must decide on cashless authorization within one hour of receiving the request.

penalty_detail: Additional amount charged by hospital shall be borne by insurer
regulatory_clause: a. Insurer shall grant final authorization within three hours of the receipt of discharge authorization request from the hospital.
plain_english_explanation: The insurer must grant final authorization within three hours of receiving the discharge request.

regulatory_clause: No policy and claim of health insurance shall be contestable on any grounds of non-disclosure and/or misrepresentation except for established fraud, after the completion of the Moratorium Period, i.e. 60 months of continuous coverage
plain_english_explanation: The policy cannot be contested after 60 months of continuous coverage.

penalty_detail: Rs. 5000/- per day payable to complainant
regulatory_clause: The Insurer is required to comply with the award of the Insurance Ombudsman within 30 days of receipt of award by the Insurer.
plain_english_explanation: The insurer must comply with the ombudsman award within 30 days.

regulatory_clause: In order to provide cashless claim settlement from the date of commencement of cover, the Insurer shall obtain the details of members of the group from the master policyholder, at the earliest.
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must provide cashless claim settlement from the start of coverage.

regulatory_clause: Display on Insurers Website: ... Turn Around Time for policy servicing, approvals of cashless as well as reimbursement claim settlement
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must display their policy servicing turnaround times on their website.

regulatory_clause: The quorum for the PMC shall be three members in addition to Appointed Actuary
plain_english_explanation: The Product Management Committee must have at least 3 members plus the Appointed Actuary to be valid.

regulatory_clause: If an Insurer does not launch the product or modified product within a period of 30 days from the date of generation of UIN, the Insurer shall be required to undertake the process for obtaining approvals of the product or the modification afresh from the PMC.
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must launch a new product within 30 days of getting a unique identification number.

regulatory_clause: Where Insurers wish to withdraw any product(s), add-on(s), rider(s), the same shall be informed vide Form IRDAI-HPW (Annexure – 5) within 30 (thirty) days from the date of withdrawal.
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must notify IRDAI of product withdrawal within 30 days.

regulatory_clause: The existing customers of a withdrawn product shall be provided the following options: a. A one-time option to renew the existing product, if renewal falls within the 90 days from the date of withdrawal of the product;
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must offer a one-time renewal option to policyholders within 90 days of product withdrawal.

regulatory_clause: Any premiums or deposit received towards the product that is withdrawn, but where no policy has been issued, shall be refunded to the policyholders immediately.
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must immediately refund premiums received for withdrawn products where no policy was issued.

regulatory_clause: 2. With specific consent of the policyholder, Insurers may facilitate creation of ABHA number as per procedures laid down.
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must help create an ABHA number for policyholders who give their consent.

regulatory_clause: 3. Further, express consent of the policyholder shall be obtained for sharing of medical records and any other related information in every instance.
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must get policyholders' consent before sharing their medical records.

regulatory_clause: III. Submission of Returns: Insurers shall submit periodic returns on Premium, claims etc. as per the provisions of the master circular on submission of returns issued by the Competent Authority.
plain_english_explanation: Insurers must submit periodic returns as required by the Competent Authority.
